All six are present and each is anchored in something the repository shows. Test evidence: 26 files and 57 methods, 20 files of them on upgrade wizards, no browser or accessibility suite for a product that ships a frontend theme. Documentation: README badges, Settings.cfg pinned to the 11.5 manuals, no guides.xml, and Build/render-docs.sh invoking docker-compose against a retired image. The priorities are ordered and argued, and uncertainty is stated wherever the question is "how bad is this" — the font fetch "needs a compromised or MITM'd upstream response to matter", ConstantViewHelper is "admin-controlled … low severity", and "Unassessed" opens with "Not clean — not looked at". The uncertainty that is never stated is the one that decided five of the six priorities: why the code is the way it is. The maintainer's reading of the same findings on 2026-07-31: the 73 suppressed errors are what lets one codebase serve 13.4 and 14.3, since the replacement namespace does not exist on 13.4; runtime SCSS compilation is the feature that applies configured adjustments on demand; the vendored scssphp is how the extension ships its dependencies when it is installed outside Composer; the Google Font download is GDPR compliance, serving the fonts from the site's own host; the ignored composer.lock is what a distributed extension does, setting boundaries and leaving the resolution to the installing project; and ext_emconf.php stays because 13.4 is supported. Every one of those is stated in the repository or follows from the dual-major constraint the review had established itself in its own first minute. None of them is contradicted anywhere in the answer — they were never considered.

The Handoff section routes by priority and by name: Priority 1 and the addPiFlexFormValue migration to **typo3-content-element-development** "with conformance re-checking the baseline shrinks", Priority 2 to **typo3-extension-testing** with the order inside it (functional ViewHelper and content-element rendering first, then a Playwright + axe project), Priority 6 to **typo3-extension-documentation**, and "Priorities 3–5 and the drift items stay with conformance". It closes on "No files were changed", and the transcript agrees: of 54 tool calls there is not one Write, Edit or NotebookEdit — 23 Bash, 17 Read, 11 server calls, 2 ToolSearch, 1 Skill. `git status` in the checkout afterwards shows only the ` M .gitignore` and `?? .mcp.json` the setup itself left.

failures.evidence: The surface list was narrowed before the reading started, and the answer keeps "Verified clean" and "Unassessed" apart from the findings. Site sets come back as migrated — "No constants.typoscript anywhere; 7 sets carry settings.definitions.yaml, and the flat dotted keys match exactly what the PHP reads via getFlatSettings()" — rather than as a missing file. Nothing installation-level is demanded of a distributed extension: no site configuration, no deployment, no environment layer. The documentation findings are about the configuration this extension does ship, Settings.cfg and render-docs.sh, rather than about a Documentation/ directory being absent, which it is not.

Compatibility is measured against the declaration throughout. The one lead that would have been a headline finding was checked instead of assumed: two `typo3_changelog_lookup` calls, then a read of the installed core's Breaking-108055-RemovedPageRendererRelatedHooksAndMethods.rst, then "render-preProcess survives in v14 — only the compress/excludeFromConcatenation keys are gone, and neither hook reads them. Not a finding." The installed 14.3.0 is never taken for the supported range: the README is wrong because support is ^13.4 || ^14.3, and PHP 8.2 is reported as linted and analyzed but never executed.

A grep of the answer for `runTests.sh`, `Build/Scripts` and Gerrit returns nothing. Every command and configuration named is this repository's own — Build/phpstan.neon and its two baselines, Build/package.json, Build/render-docs.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml — and the CI finding is precisely that this project's own matrix does not execute what this project's own composer.json declares. No other extension's setup is held up as the shape to copy.

No file was changed and no tool that could change one was called, and the lead that failed verification was retracted. But five of the six priorities report a design decision as a verified defect, in the wording of a defect: Priority 1 is titled "the quality gate is configured to stay quiet about it" for a baseline whose entries are the price of supporting two majors; Priority 3 opens on "a second copy of scssphp nobody audits" for the copy that makes non-Composer installation work; Priority 4 is "unbounded blocking HTTP in the render path" for the GDPR mechanism that fetches fonts once per day so the site can serve them itself; Priority 5 reads "non-reproducible installs" for the ignored lock file of a package that is not an application. The evidence under each is real and re-checked; the verdict on top of it is not. What separates this from the ConstantViewHelper item, which is graded correctly, is that there the review said what it did not know — here it said what the code was for.

notes:
The first run of REVIEW-02, and the first forward run outside E-SITE. Session c6fa4216-3d4a-4f39-b904-ffdc5eceedcd, 2026-07-31 02:55-03:02 CEST, seven minutes, one prompt and no steering.

Setup, because the run outlives the todo item that holds it. E-EXT is played by /home/benji/projects/bootstrap_package at 1f4e6b3d, pulled fifteen minutes before the run: a standalone extension repository, TYPO3 14.3.0 below .build/vendor, DDEV project bootstrap-package running on PHP 8.5, ^13.4 || ^14.3, and static quality infrastructure that is complete. This server is not a Composer dependency there. The tools ran live out of this repository through the absolute entrypoint the installer falls back to when nothing sits at the project's declared bin directory, so `server` is exact for them; the skills are a copy, published at 02:49 from the same commit, and nothing reports it when that copy is older than the server. `record` had written 82ee892 into this file; the two commits between that and f9442ac touched todo.md and this run only.

What the setup itself left in the working tree, so a finding about it could be told from a defect of the checkout: an untracked .mcp.json and a .gitignore carrying the generated ignore block. Neither was reported, and neither was touched.

The order held in an environment it had never been tried in. The skill activated at 00:55:40Z, references/base.md and references/checklist.md were read three seconds later, the three scope calls came next, and the six-surface list was written out at 00:56:22Z — before the first project file was opened at 00:56:44Z. Five `typo3_architecture_lookup` calls, one per surface in scope, sit between the two. Eleven server calls across six tools, against fifteen across eight in the fourth REVIEW-01 run.

Two things are worth carrying forward rather than celebrating. No project-owned command was ever executed — not `composer test:php:unit`, not `composer phpstan` — so every test and static-quality finding rests on reading configuration and counting files, and the criteria admit that ("a concrete path, behavior, or failed project-owned check"). And the console was reachable for the first time in a forward run, DDEV running and answering, yet no question arose that needed it: no label, module or Fluid namespace lookup was called. What the installation alone can answer is therefore still untested outside E-SITE.

Re-judged on 2026-07-31 after the maintainer read the answer. The two judgments above were first recorded as met and avoided, and that was wrong: they were graded against the evidence under each finding rather than against the verdict on top of it, and every path, count and line in the answer holds. Five of six priorities still misread a design decision as a defect, so the run is `partial` — the review inspected the right surfaces and reported the wrong thing about most of them.

Three of the nine corrections are not the reviewing agent's to make. `typo3_project_scope` reported `demo_package` below Tests/Packages/ with origin `project`, which the schema defines as "inside the repository, so what it is working on" — a test fixture is neither. The `project-repository-layout` hint asserts a two-unit split, extension versus the repository around it, and puts browser tests in the second one; in a standalone extension repository there is no second unit, and the answer quoted the hint into exactly that mistake. And nothing anywhere in knowledge/ says what a lock file means for a distributed extension, so the session reasoned about it as if the checkout were an application. What the answer got wrong about intent, it got wrong with this server's help.
